units.title: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation

questions.stem: An electric dipole consists of charges +q and −q separated by a distance 2a. What is the electric field at the centre of the dipole?

options.label: A
options.text: zero, because the net charge of the dipole is zero

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): At large distances the electric field of an electric dipole falls off faster than the field of a single point charge.
Reason (R): The two charges of a dipole are equal and opposite, so their fields almost cancel at distant points.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the electric field.
A. It is a vector quantity.
B. The field of an isolated point charge has the same magnitude at all points of a sphere centred on the charge.
C. The field of an isolated positive point charge points towards the charge.
D. The field due to several charges is the vector sum of the fields due to the individual charges.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

Consider the following statements about electric flux.
A. Electric flux is a scalar quantity.
B. The net flux through a closed surface due to a charge lying outside the surface is zero.
C. The flux through a surface depends on the orientation of the surface relative to the field.
D. The net flux through any closed surface is always positive.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
Two large parallel plane sheets carry uniform surface charge densities of +8.85 × 10⁻⁸ C m⁻² and −8.85 × 10⁻⁸ C m⁻². What is the electric field between the sheets and outside them?

options.label: A
options.text: 10⁴ N C⁻¹ between the sheets and zero outside

options.label: B
options.text: 5 × 10³ N C⁻¹ between the sheets and zero outside

options.label: C
options.text: zero between the sheets and 10⁴ N C⁻¹ outside

options.label: D
options.text: 10⁴ N C⁻¹ both between and outside the sheets

questions.stem: A 4 μF capacitor charged to 50 V is disconnected from the supply and connected across an identical uncharged 4 μF capacitor. How much energy is lost in the process?
A negative point charge is placed at a point where the electric field points towards the east. In which direction does the electric force on the charge act?

options.label: A
options.text: Towards the east, along the field, because the field alone fixes the direction of force on any charge

options.label: B
options.text: Towards the west, opposite to the field, because the force is $\vec F = q\vec E$ and $q$ is negative

options.label: C
options.text: Towards the north, perpendicular to the field, because a negative charge is deflected sideways by it

options.label: D
options.text: No force acts on it, because the negative sign of the charge cancels the effect of the field on it

questions.stem: Which one of the following materials is paramagnetic?

options.label: A
options.text: Copper, whose atoms have permanent magnetic moments that line up very strongly along an applied field

options.label: B
options.text: Aluminium, whose atoms have permanent magnetic moments that are only weakly aligned by a field

options.label: C
options.text: Bismuth, whose atoms have permanent magnetic moments that are always aligned against an applied field

options.label: D
options.text: Iron, whose atoms have no permanent magnetic moments at all and acquire them only in an applied field

A. Glass has a larger refractive index for violet light than for red light.
B. In vacuum, violet light travels more slowly than red light.

questions.unit: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.stem:
Read the following statements about photons:
A. The energy of a photon depends on the frequency of the radiation and not on its intensity.
B. Photons are deflected by electric and magnetic fields because they carry energy.
C. In a collision between a photon and an electron, the total energy and the total momentum are conserved.
D. The total number of photons is conserved in every interaction of radiation with matter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

Among the Balmer-series transitions drawn in the energy-level diagram, which one emits the photon of greatest energy?

Consider the following statements about the spectrum of hydrogen:
A. Within each series, the lines crowd closer together towards the short-wavelength end (the series limit).
B. The first line of the Lyman series has a longer wavelength than the first line of the Balmer series.
C. When white light containing ultraviolet passes through cool hydrogen gas, the absorption lines observed are mainly those of the Lyman series.
D. Every photon of the Balmer series has energy less than 3.4 eV.
Which of the statements are correct?

C. Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers.
D. ${}^{2}_{1}\text{H}$ and ${}^{3}_{2}\text{He}$ are isotones.
Which of the statements are correct?

Assertion (A): Silicon is a semiconductor, whereas diamond, which has a similar crystal structure, is an insulator.

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem: Why does a capacitor connected in parallel with the load reduce the ripple in the output of a rectifier?

options.label: A
options.text: It charges to nearly the peak voltage while the diode conducts and then discharges slowly through the load as the rectified voltage falls, filling in the gaps between pulses

options.label: B
options.text: It blocks the DC component and passes only the AC component to the load

options.label: C
options.text: It raises the frequency of the AC mains so that the pulses come faster

options.label: D
options.text: It reverses the polarity of every second output pulse

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about energy bands.
A. In metals the conduction band is partly filled or overlaps the valence band.
B. In semiconductors the forbidden gap is small, of the order of 1 eV or so.
C. In insulators the forbidden gap is large, greater than about 3 eV.
D. In semiconductors the number of free charge carriers decreases as the temperature rises.
Choose the correct option.
